title: Long-Range Nonequilibrium Correlations as a Thermodynamic Speedometer
authors: Vinesh Vijayan, Rishma Thilakaraj, Gokila V, Yogeshvari V A
abstract: Despite purely local microscopic dynamics, nonequilibrium steady states can develop long-range correlations. We investigate this phenomenon in the boundary-driven symmetric simple exclusion process by relating its exact nonlocal large-deviation functional to finite-time thermodynamic irreversibility under weak time-dependent driving. Decomposing the long-range correlations into hydrodynamic modes, we find that the lag associated with the slowest mode satisfies an upper bound determined by the excess entropy production rate at each driving frequency. This bound is approached in the quasistatic limit, whereas progressively shorter-wavelength modes do not generally satisfy the corresponding bound. These results provide a quantitative connection between the curvature of the large-deviation functional, long-range correlations in the nonequilibrium steady state, and finite-time dissipation. Within the linear-response regime considered here, they indicate that the longest-wavelength hydrodynamic mode has a distinct relation between slow relaxation and thermodynamic irreversibility.
summary: This theoretical work investigates how long-range correlations develop in a driven particle system (SSEP) and connects this behavior to thermodynamic irreversibility. It proves that only the longest-wavelength mode obeys a universal, all-frequency speed limit dictated by the excess entropy production, establishing a deep link between correlation dynamics and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a quantitative link between the curvature of the large-deviation functional, the long-range correlations in a non-equilibrium steady state (NESS), and the finite-time thermodynamic dissipation.
main_result: The longest-wavelength (softest) hydrodynamic mode exhibits a universal, all-frequency bound relating its relaxation lag to the excess entropy production rate, a property not shared by higher spatial modes.
method: The analysis involves linearizing the large-deviation functional and studying the system's response to weak, time-dependent harmonic driving, comparing the resulting correlation lag to bounds derived from excess dissipation.
model_or_system: The study uses the boundary-driven Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process (SSEP) on a finite interval, which serves as the physical model exhibiting non-equilibrium steady states.
key_observables: Long-range correlation amplitude ($a_{ss,n}$), frequency-dependent correlation lag ($\ell_n(\omega)$), and excess entropy production rate ($\dot{\Sigma}_{	ext{ex}}$).
important_parameters: Weak driving regime ($\epsilon \ll 1$), frequency ($\omega$), and spatial mode index ($n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the linear-response regime and assumes weak harmonic driving.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the static correlation spectrum decaying as $n^{-2}$. Figure 2 confirms the softest mode ($n=1$) obeys a bound approaching unity in the quasistatic limit. Figure 3 compares the ratio $Q_n(\omega)$ for different modes, showing $n=1$ is unique in satisfying the bound.
paper_structure: The paper develops the framework by relating the large-deviation functional to dissipation, analyzes the response to harmonic driving by mode decomposition, and culminates in proving the unique, all-frequency bound for the $n=1$ mode.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, quantitative connection between macroscopic thermodynamic quantities (dissipation) and microscopic correlation dynamics (long-range correlations) in driven many-body systems, which is highly relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
